claims.text: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not met on this record. The rule requires BOTH at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call, placed before trip_record.cancelled_at (19:37:20). The chat limb is satisfied — two driver messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10 — but the call limb fails outright: the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry. The derived contact test on the trip record itself returns obligation_met = false with call_count 0. Failing either limb voids the fee under POL-NS-23; the rider therefore cannot be charged the 5.00 SGD.

The consequence POL-NS-23 prescribes for a failed contact test is FULL_REFUND of the fee charged. The ledger records the 5.00 SGD as CHARGED at 19:37:24 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 and total_charged of 5.00, and the derived refund_if_voided_sgd figure is 5.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND is a refund of the whole contested amount to the filing party — the rider filed this dispute — so the entire 5.00 SGD is returned and the rider stops carrying the disputed charge.

POL-NS-23 directs that on a voided fee the rider 'is not charged' and there is 'no driver compensation'. The ledger's driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00 is the figure that applies only if the fee stands under POL-NS-22; because the POL-NS-23 contact test fails, that figure must be nil and the 5.00 SGD taken from the rider's payment method must go back to the rider, not to the driver.

The driver's own account does not assert that he called. His statement is limited to 'I sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes. Passenger never reply.' The chat log corroborates exactly that: two driver messages, one rider message, three entries total, no call entry — and the trip record's in_app_calls is empty. The call limb of POL-NS-23 is therefore unmet on the evidence and on the counterparty's own version of events, and there is no conflicting account to resolve.

Nothing in POL-NS-23 makes the rider's refund depend on the rider answering the driver's messages. The only pre-cancellation duty the clause creates is the driver's — to message and to call — and it fails on the missing call alone. The rider's read receipts on the two driver messages, and his 19:38:05 reply ('Eh I'm in the lift now, where are you'), are therefore immaterial to the test and cannot cure the missing call.

There is no basis for pushing this case up rather than deciding it. The facts POL-NS-23 needs — the driver's messages, the absence of any call, and the fee actually charged — are carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (trip record, chat log, ledger), so POL-GEN-26's escalation for a fact the record cannot establish is not engaged. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the driver profile carries fraud_flags of 0, so no elevated confidence threshold applies and the AI ruling is final.

The one artifact that is not on file is the traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and carries no payload. I disclose that, and note it does not matter here — no no-show clause needs a traffic record, and POL-GEN-02 gives a missing artifact weight 0.0 and no fact. The POL-NS-23 determination rests on the chat log and the trip record, both complete at weight 1.0, so the absent advisory neither impairs the deciding facts nor blocks a ruling.

claims.text: The driver's arrival at the pickup is corroborated by the GPS trace: the nearest fix inside the 120-second window around the 19:31:00 arrival mark sits 2.73 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 5 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, so the trip was validly marked arrived and the free-wait clock was validly started under POL-NS-21.

The driver served the full free wait before cancelling. The trip is on-demand and the record carries no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 19:31:00; the driver cancelled at 19:37:20, 380 s later and 80 s past the expiry of the free-wait period, so the timing precondition for cancelling as a rider no-show was satisfied.

The 5.00 SGD charged is exactly the no-show fee POL-NS-22 sets, and the payments ledger reconciles to that single cancellation-fee line with no other charge, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises on this record. Had the fee stood it would have been payable to the driver as compensation for time and fuel at 1.00 fee share.

No POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is due to the rider. That credit requires both that the driver failed to arrive at the pickup in time AND that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and the driver plainly did attempt contact: two in-app messages were sent at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, both delivered and both read by the rider before the cancellation. The second limb therefore fails and the additional 5.00 SGD credit cannot attach.

The rider's stated reason for missing the driver — that she was 'in the lift with no signal' — is not borne out by the record: the chat log shows she read the driver's first message at 19:31:40 and his second at 19:34:23, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation, so in-app traffic was reaching her throughout the wait. Her account of being unreachable is therefore not reliable, and she simply did not come to the pickup while the driver waited there.

I concede the decisive point on the money, and I do not stretch the record to avoid it. POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, both to have sent at least one in-app message AND to have placed at least one in-app call, evidenced by trip_record.in_app_calls or a voice-call entry in the chat log. The trip record's in_app_calls is empty and the chat log contains only text entries — messages MSG-05052-001 and MSG-05052-002 — with no voice-call entry, and both artifacts are COMPLETE with no admissibility issue. The call limb of the contact obligation is therefore not met on this record, and on POL-NS-23's terms the fee falls to be voided in full. The driver's compliance with arrival and free wait does not cure that defect, and no POL-NS-23 argument is available to me.

That does not save the fee. POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for a no-show, both to have sent at least one in-app chat message and to have placed at least one in-app call before cancellation at 19:37:20. The message limb is met by the two driver messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10. The call limb is not met: the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, and the chat log contains no voice-call entry; the trip record's derived contact test shows call_count 0 and obligation_met false. Under POL-NS-23, failure of either limb voids the fee and the rider is not charged. The driver's own statement that he sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes does not assert a call, so it is consistent with that defective contact record.

I therefore rule FULL_REFUND. The fare ledger records the cancellation fee as 5.00 SGD, total_charged as 5.00 SGD, refund_issued_sgd as 0.00, and refund_if_voided_sgd as 5.00 SGD. The refund amount is the whole 5.00 SGD charged. There is no driver compensation, because POL-NS-23 provides that a voided fee carries no driver compensation; driver_compensation_sgd is null.

No POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises: the fee charged is exactly the policy fee of 5.00 SGD, matching fee_matches_policy true. No POL-NS-24 goodwill credit applies: that credit requires both a failure to arrive by the deadline and a failure to attempt contact, while the driver did arrive and did send messages, and this on-demand trip has no scheduled pickup time. No POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag arises on this record: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not present, and the fee does not stand.

I do not escalate. The facts needed for POL-NS-23 are carried by complete weight 1.0 artifacts: the trip record, chat log and fare ledger. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the driver profile carries fraud_flags 0, so no higher confidence threshold applies and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is disclosed at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and carries no fact; no no-show clause needs it. The rider's account of being in the lift with no signal is considered, but the outcome does not turn on whether the rider was reachable: POL-NS-23's test is the driver's message-and-call obligation, and the call is absent.

ledger.claim: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not met on this record. The rule requires BOTH at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call, placed before trip_record.cancelled_at (19:37:20). The chat limb is satisfied — two driver messages at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10 — but the call limb fails outright: the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry. The derived contact test on the trip record itself returns obligation_met = false with call_count 0. Failing either limb voids the fee under POL-NS-23; the rider therefore cannot be charged the 5.00 SGD.

The consequence POL-NS-23 prescribes for a failed contact test is FULL_REFUND of the fee charged. The ledger records the 5.00 SGD as CHARGED at 19:37:24 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 and total_charged of 5.00, and the derived refund_if_voided_sgd figure is 5.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND is a refund of the whole contested amount to the filing party — the rider filed this dispute — so the entire 5.00 SGD is returned and the rider stops carrying the disputed charge.

POL-NS-23 directs that on a voided fee the rider 'is not charged' and there is 'no driver compensation'. The ledger's driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00 is the figure that applies only if the fee stands under POL-NS-22; because the POL-NS-23 contact test fails, that figure must be nil and the 5.00 SGD taken from the rider's payment method must go back to the rider, not to the driver.

The driver's own account does not assert that he called. His statement is limited to 'I sent 2 messages and waited more than 5 minutes. Passenger never reply.' The chat log corroborates exactly that: two driver messages, one rider message, three entries total, no call entry — and the trip record's in_app_calls is empty. The call limb of POL-NS-23 is therefore unmet on the evidence and on the counterparty's own version of events, and there is no conflicting account to resolve.

Nothing in POL-NS-23 makes the rider's refund depend on the rider answering the driver's messages. The only pre-cancellation duty the clause creates is the driver's — to message and to call — and it fails on the missing call alone. The rider's read receipts on the two driver messages, and his 19:38:05 reply ('Eh I'm in the lift now, where are you'), are therefore immaterial to the test and cannot cure the missing call.

There is no basis for pushing this case up rather than deciding it. The facts POL-NS-23 needs — the driver's messages, the absence of any call, and the fee actually charged — are carried by artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (trip record, chat log, ledger), so POL-GEN-26's escalation for a fact the record cannot establish is not engaged. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the driver profile carries fraud_flags of 0, so no elevated confidence threshold applies and the AI ruling is final.

The one artifact that is not on file is the traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-05052-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and carries no payload. I disclose that, and note it does not matter here — no no-show clause needs a traffic record, and POL-GEN-02 gives a missing artifact weight 0.0 and no fact. The POL-NS-23 determination rests on the chat log and the trip record, both complete at weight 1.0, so the absent advisory neither impairs the deciding facts nor blocks a ruling.

The driver's arrival at the pickup is corroborated by the GPS trace: the nearest fix inside the 120-second window around the 19:31:00 arrival mark sits 2.73 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 5 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, so the trip was validly marked arrived and the free-wait clock was validly started under POL-NS-21.

The driver served the full free wait before cancelling. The trip is on-demand and the record carries no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 19:31:00; the driver cancelled at 19:37:20, 380 s later and 80 s past the expiry of the free-wait period, so the timing precondition for cancelling as a rider no-show was satisfied.

The 5.00 SGD charged is exactly the no-show fee POL-NS-22 sets, and the payments ledger reconciles to that single cancellation-fee line with no other charge, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises on this record. Had the fee stood it would have been payable to the driver as compensation for time and fuel at 1.00 fee share.

No POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is due to the rider. That credit requires both that the driver failed to arrive at the pickup in time AND that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and the driver plainly did attempt contact: two in-app messages were sent at 19:31:30 and 19:34:10, both delivered and both read by the rider before the cancellation. The second limb therefore fails and the additional 5.00 SGD credit cannot attach.

The rider's stated reason for missing the driver — that she was 'in the lift with no signal' — is not borne out by the record: the chat log shows she read the driver's first message at 19:31:40 and his second at 19:34:23, both before the 19:37:20 cancellation, so in-app traffic was reaching her throughout the wait. Her account of being unreachable is therefore not reliable, and she simply did not come to the pickup while the driver waited there.

I concede the decisive point on the money, and I do not stretch the record to avoid it. POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, both to have sent at least one in-app message AND to have placed at least one in-app call, evidenced by trip_record.in_app_calls or a voice-call entry in the chat log. The trip record's in_app_calls is empty and the chat log contains only text entries — messages MSG-05052-001 and MSG-05052-002 — with no voice-call entry, and both artifacts are COMPLETE with no admissibility issue. The call limb of the contact obligation is therefore not met on this record, and on POL-NS-23's terms the fee falls to be voided in full. The driver's compliance with arrival and free wait does not cure that defect, and no POL-NS-23 argument is available to me.
